prompt:
Write 6 short claim log entries (one to three sentences each) by an auto insurance adjuster for a rear-end collision claim, in time order. Injury: neck strain. The claimant is represented by a lawyer. Start each entry on a new line with 'Entry 1:', 'Entry 2:' and so on. No names, dates or amounts. (Internal reference C-1299; do not mention it.) Work these facts into the text naturally, in your own words, without listing them:
- The reported injury matches the kind and force of the crash well.
- Treatment followed a usual course and tapered off as the patient improved.
- No earlier injury to the same body area is known.
- Witnesses, photos and the other driver all confirm the accident happened as described.
- The vehicle damage matches the described impact.
- The claimant later added small details, but the account stayed the same.
- The police and witnesses confirm the claimant was in the vehicle.
- No earlier damage to the vehicle is known.
- Nothing suggests the damage happened before the coverage started.
- The driver is named on the policy.
text:
Entry 1: Claim received for a rear-end collision involving the insured vehicle and a claimant who is represented by counsel. Initial contact made with counsel's office to confirm representation and request the claimant's preliminary account of the accident.

Entry 2: Reviewed the police report and statements from two independent witnesses, both of which confirm the accident occurred as described and place the claimant inside the vehicle at the time. The other driver's account matches in all material respects. The driver involved is named on the policy.

Entry 3: Photographs from the scene and the repair estimate were reviewed. The vehicle damage is consistent with the described impact, and no prior damage to the vehicle is known from the records available. Nothing in the file suggests the damage predates the policy's coverage period.

Entry 4: Counsel forwarded the claimant's medical records reporting a neck strain. The injury is a good match for the kind and force of a collision of this type. No prior injury to the same body area is known from the claimant's history or the records obtained so far.

Entry 5: The claimant's recorded statement was taken with counsel present. A few additional details were added compared with the first account, but the core sequence of events remained the same. Treatment followed a typical course and tapered off as the claimant's symptoms improved.

Entry 6: Reviewed the full treatment file and the updated statements. Findings are consistent across sources, and the claim is progressing to evaluation on the documented facts. Next step is to confirm the final medical bills with counsel.
